answer: Every identity faces a voiceprint challenge: the operator reads a random phrase, and the system checks the voice embedding against a registry of embeddings. First, the registry rejects any embedding within 0.95 cosine similarity of an existing one, so one voice yields no clone. Second, the phrase changes each epoch, so recordings cannot be replayed. Third, 5% get a human re-check; a mismatch burns the bond. 100 voice actors at  each cost 00 per 100 fakes. Like a canyon holding one river, a glacier holding its own meltwater, shale splitting on one seam, each voice enters once.
